generation.mechanism: Short-range order should reduce lattice distortion and phonon scattering, modify the high-frequency phonon density of states, and create high-conductivity percolation pathways whose benefit outweighs scattering from the ordered regions themselves.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the random state, lattice thermal conductivity should rise by approximately 12%, while atomic displacements should decline by roughly 12–13%.

generation.boundary: The hypothesis may extend to other bcc or fcc high-entropy alloys only when specific ordered binary clusters percolate; it will not imply the strong temperature-dependent conductivity decrease typical of random fcc alloys.
generation.uncertainty: The main uncertainty will be whether simulated clusters reach the connectivity needed for percolation within the constrained single-phase model.
